blurb: The city of Socrates, Plato and the first democracy.

facts.t: Socrates was tried by a jury of 501 citizens in 399 BC and sentenced to death. Tourists are shown a cave on Philopappos Hill as his prison, but that is a legend; the real state prison was probably in the Agora.

Plato taught in a grove outside the walls named after the hero Academus, which gave us the word academy. His pupil Aristotle later opened his own school, the Lyceum; its ruins were found in 1996 when digging for a new museum.
In 1896 the first modern Olympic Games were held in the Panathenaic Stadium, rebuilt in marble on the ancient site.
